transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Hundreds of thousands of customers across the southeast are still without electricity.
After Hurricane Isaias made landfall along the Florida panhandle last night.
At least two deaths are blamed on the storm.
Pat Duggan's of Alabama Public Radio reports the storm's been downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.
But it is dumping heavy rain as it makes its way north.
The National Weather Service says what's left of Isaias will make its way through Tennessee and Kentucky as a depression after making landfall at Destin, Florida overnight.
The system's expected to drop four to eight inches of rain over the southeast with possible flash flooding along the Gulf Coast of Alabama and Florida.
Mobile County Emergency Manager Mike Evans told residents not to rely on social media during Isaias.
I don't understand it. I know on social media with algorithms, sometimes if you look at something, it could be from 12 hours ago.
Isaias broke the record setback in 1905 as the latest hurricane has formed during an Atlantic storm season.
For NPR News, I'm Pat Duggan in Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
President Trump says Russia will supply possibly millions of tons of diesel to the U.S., undercutting U.S. sanctions, which the U.S. now says it's lifting.
Trump says it's an effort to lower rising diesel prices. And here's Emily Fang has more.
It's unclear if importing Russian diesel flies in the face of a new law Trump just signed into effect.
Named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the law put 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports and personally sanctioned Putin.
The U.S. Treasury Department has, however, just temporarily paused its sanctions on Russian diesel.
Trump has also temporarily paused a federal tax on diesel, though some state taxes may still remain, all in an effort to rein in diesel prices that have shot up as much as 70 percent since the war with Iran.
These measures will likely not bring diesel prices down, however.
For example, the diesel Russia will provide amounts to just a few days of American national diesel consumption.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump has selected a new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, succeeding Caroline Levitt, who left the job in August.
NPR's Deepa Shiberam has more.
Zacharia is a political commentator and an adviser with Trump's media and technology group, which runs Trump's social media site, Truth Social.
She also briefly served as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security.
It's not clear when her first day in the role would be or when the first press briefing would be. Those briefings have largely been on hold since Levitt left the position earlier this year.
Trump's selection of a new press secretary comes as the president and his party are facing headwinds in the upcoming midterm elections.
On social media, Trump says he's confident Zacharia will deliver "strong results for our country" and calls her a loyal and brilliant supporter.
Deepa Shiberam, NPR News, The White House.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
In India, security forces have shut down central New Delhi and detained protest leaders to prevent demonstrations.
And, here's Deha Deed reports, the protests are targeting a controversial revision of voter lists that has removed millions of names.
Police boarded a flight that had just landed, carrying protest leaders.
One leader, Abhijit Deepke, says in a video he shared online,
Police also drag barricades across roads that lead to a protest site.
This bled over a loudspeaker.
Police say they're preventing disorder.
The protests are over a controversial revision of voter rolls that has crossed millions of people off electoral lists.
Critics allege the government is trying to disenfranchise voters who are unlikely to vote for the ruling Hindu Nationalist Party led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The government has not responded to those accusations.
Deha Deed, NPR News, New Delhi.
President Trump is continuing to try to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook by establishing what's called a committee of inquiry yesterday to investigate allegations that she made false statements on mortgage applications.
The extraordinary move follows the Supreme Court ruling in June that Cook could keep her job after Trump tried to fire her last year.
That ruling found that Cook should have had notice and an opportunity to respond to the charges.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.
This message comes from U.S. Bank.
Chief Product Officer Shruti Patel shares why U.S. Bank Business Essentials is designed to bring together the key products small business owners need.
Some of our small business owners were telling us how complicated it was, having checking in one place, built by in another.
And so our goal was to help business owners bring it all together by building business essentials.
This was really to help business owners focus more on growing their business.

topics.text: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida panhandle, leaving hundreds of thousands without power and two dead
Trump says Russia will supply diesel to U.S., temporarily pausing Russian diesel sanctions and a federal diesel tax
Trump selects Katie Zacharia as new White House press secretary, succeeding Caroline Levitt
India security forces shut down central New Delhi and detain protest leaders over voter roll revision
Trump launches committee of inquiry to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage statements
